problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}[A\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -3 & 1 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 &  &  &  \\ 0 & 1 & 0 &  &  &  \\ 0 & 0 & 1 &  &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

examples.problem:
The inverse of the $3 \times 3$ matrix $K$ is found using row operations, as shown below. Complete the process, and determine $K^{-1}.$

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 &  &  &  \\ 0 & 1 & 0 &  &  &  \\ 0 & 0 & 1 &  &  & \end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
examples.worked_solution:
We write down $K$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $K$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[K\,|\,I\,] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 3 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 & -5 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{5}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The matrix $K^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore,

feedback.problem:
Which of the following matrices are transformed into the $3\times 3$ identity matrix after applying the row operations ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\,$ and $\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2}?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's apply the operations to each of the matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -5 & 0 \\ -5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-5 & -25 & 0 \\ 0 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times  \\ B & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =I\,✓ \\ C & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+5{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne I\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$B$ only".
